surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Mercer scores against his old team
paras: Dawson Mercer opened the scoring for the Jets early in the first, in his first game against New Jersey since leaving. Kyle Connor pushed the lead to 2-0 on the power play late in the period. Jesper Bratt and Cody Glass scored 44 seconds apart early in the second to tie it 2-2, but that was the last goal the Devils would get. The Devils went more than 17 minutes without a shot on goal, from late in the second to midway through the third, even with a power play in that stretch. Mercer scored again on the power play midway through the third to put the Jets ahead for good. Connor scored again into the empty net with just under a minute left.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Nico Daws made 19 saves for the Jets, and Jake Allen stopped 21 of 24 at the other end.
The Jets killed all four Devils power plays. The Jets improved to 8-8-3, sixth in the Central, while the Devils fell to 13-6-0, second in the Metropolitan.
